decisions.reason: The Windows CommandLineToArgvW test double returns the supplied argv array but hard-codes argc.value to four. Its five-token negative case is therefore truncated to four tokens before production evaluates it. The real API supplies the actual parsed count, and production already predicates acceptance on len(argv) == 4. The failed assertion is deterministic fixture misinformation, not evidence of a production authorization or containment gap.
expanded_evidence: orchestrator_harness/tests/test_firmware_c3_harness.py:491-495 fixes Count.value at 4 for every supplied argv
orchestrator_harness/tests/test_firmware_c3_harness.py:499-500 supplies a five-token negative case through that fixed-count fake
firmware_acceptance/c3_process_identity.py:33-35 requires exactly four parsed entries and the exact remaining module argv
decisions.smallest_fix: In the test-only fake, report len(argv) through the Count constructor used by that matches call; preserve all positive and negative cases and change no production source.
decisions.complexity_and_risk: Very low; a local test double becomes faithful to the operating-system API contract.
